transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… well, I’m here because my family and some friends keep telling me I’m wrong about my money. They say the bank papers show nothing was taken, and I know they want me to accept that, but… it’s been over a year and I just know they’re hiding it.

I don’t want to sound like I’m causing trouble or anything. I’ve just had to keep asking them, confronting them, because there’s been bills and fundraisers and even trip plans that feel like they’re being used to cover it up. I just need someone to understand that I’m not making it up.
Can you tell me more about why you believe your family and friends are hiding the missing money from you?

I mean… I know it probably sounds like I’m being difficult, and I don’t want you to think I’m trying to accuse people for no reason. But they keep pointing to the bank papers like that’s supposed to settle it, and it doesn’t. Those papers don’t show what I know happened.

For over a year, I’ve felt like they’ve been moving things around or covering it up. Like when bills come up, or there’s a fundraiser, or someone starts talking about trip plans… it feels connected, like that’s where my money went or how they’re trying to explain it away. So I keep asking them, maybe more than they like, but I just need them to tell the truth. Does that make sense?
Can you describe a specific instance where you felt someone was trying to hide something from you, and how you reacted to that?

One time… I guess a clear one was when they were talking about a trip, and at the same time there were bills and some fundraiser stuff going around. They kept saying the bank papers showed nothing was missing, but it just felt like they were using all of that to explain where the money had gone.

I didn’t want to make a scene, honestly. I know it can sound bad. But I asked them again, and I probably pushed more than they wanted. I told them I knew they were hiding it and that I needed them to just tell me the truth. Is that… is that the kind of example you mean?

Can you explain what you meant when you said they’re hiding your money and using bills, fundraisers, and trips to cover it up? Do you believe they’re working together in a coordinated way to deceive you?

I don’t want to say it like… like they’re all sitting in a room planning it, because I know that sounds extreme. But yes, I do feel like they’re working together in some way, or at least covering for each other.

The bank papers keep getting used to tell me nothing was taken, but I’ve known for over a year that my money is being hidden. Then when bills come up, or fundraisers, or trip plans, it feels like those things are being used to explain it away or cover where it went. I know I keep confronting them, and I’m not trying to be a problem, but I can’t just let it go until they tell me the truth.

You mentioned that you believe your money is being hidden despite what the bank papers say. Has this belief ever been so strong that you felt certain it was true, even when others showed you evidence that it wasn’t?

Yes… I mean, I don’t want to sound stubborn or like I’m ignoring people on purpose. But yes, it has felt that certain to me.

That’s really why I came in, because my family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, and I know they want me to accept that. But for over a year I’ve felt like I know my money is being hidden, and the bills and fundraisers and trip plans are part of how they’re covering it up. So even when they show me the papers, it doesn’t change what I know happened.

I know that probably doesn’t sound good, but I feel like I have to keep asking them until somebody tells me the truth. Is that okay to say?

Has there ever been a time when you were shown clear proof that your money wasn’t taken, such as bank statements or receipts, and even then, did you still feel completely certain that your money was being hidden from you?

Yes… that’s kind of what I mean. They’ve shown me the bank papers, and everybody keeps saying that proves nothing was taken. I understand that’s what they’re trying to show me.

But even then, I still feel like… I know my money is being hidden. It’s been over a year, and the bills and the fundraisers and the trip plans all feel like they’re being used to cover it up. I don’t want to sound difficult, but I can’t just accept it when it feels so clear to me. That’s why I keep confronting them, because I feel like someone needs to tell me the truth. Is that answering it right?
Even when people showed you the bank papers and receipts, did it ever feel like the proof they gave you was part of the cover-up instead of evidence that nothing happened?

Yes… I think so. I know that probably sounds bad, and I’m not trying to be unreasonable, but when they showed me the bank papers and receipts, it didn’t make me feel better. It felt more like that was the way they were trying to prove their story.

That’s why I came in, because my family and friends keep saying those papers prove nothing was taken. But for over a year I’ve felt like I know they’re hiding my money, and then the bills, fundraisers, and trip plans get used to cover it up or explain it away.

I don’t want to accuse people unfairly, but I keep feeling like I have to confront them until somebody tells me the truth. Does that make sense?
